Spiritborn · Hybrid

Evade Counterswarm Spiritborn - Boss Variant

poison swarm, single-target weighted

Spiritborn hybrid unchanged poison swarm, single-target weighted based on Evade Counterswarm Spiritborn

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

Move on whenHarmony of Ebewaka in hand. In the base build this is a late-endgame item; here it is the gate into the early endgame, which is the single biggest structural difference between the two pages.
Move on whenWidow's Web procing reliably and your cooldown reduction high enough that Rushing Claw's charges are back before you need them.
Move on whenA lair boss killed measurably faster than the base build manages it. If it is not faster, play spiritborn-meta-evade-counterswarm and enjoy the clear speed.

Skill bar

1Rushing Claw
2Scourge
3Counterattack
4Ravager
5Toxic Skin
6The Devourer

Rotation

Unchanged from the base build: Rushing Claw through the pack and let the orbiting swarms do the killing. At this stage you are still a speed-farmer; the boss weighting starts when Harmony of Ebewaka lands.

Skill point priority

  1. Counterattack to max with Counterattack of the Swarm - the swarms are the damage and the skill name is misleading
  2. Rushing Claw with Evasive Swipe, and remember it is a movement skill: it does not count as an Evade, so the Cem rune does nothing with it
  3. Toxic Skin and Ravager for uptime
  4. Scourge for Vulnerable and Weaken
  5. The Devourer last
  6. Variant note: cooldown reduction is the gearing problem for the whole archetype - rings, gloves, helm, amulet, plus mobility cooldown tempers on boots and amulet

Skill bar

1Rushing Claw
2Scourge
3Counterattack
4Ravager
5Toxic Skin
6The Devourer

Rotation

Rushing Claw to close, Scourge to apply Vulnerable and Weaken, then stand in the fight rather than passing through it - which is the opposite of the base build's instruction and is the whole variant. Tzic is doing the heavy lifting on anything unstoppable.

Skill point priority

  1. Counterattack maxed; Ravager and Toxic Skin maxed for uptime
  2. Scourge for Vulnerable - it matters more on a target that lives long enough for the debuff to pay
  3. Rushing Claw stays at one point plus its charge upgrades
  4. Carry enough critical strike chance to proc Widow's Web reliably, and no more: the damage is a damage-over-time and cannot crit

Rotation

Same as the early endgame. This is where the variant earns or loses its argument: time a lair boss against the base build and see whether keeping Widow's Web and the Gorilla/Eagle pairing actually pays.

Skill point priority

  1. Unchanged from the early endgame
  2. Glyph level order, published verbatim by the base guide: Consumption, Canny, Fester, Bane, Menagerist
  3. Do not reintroduce the Colossal glyph - it was pulled from the guide after being found not to work with the swarm's damage over time

Rotation

Pit floors whose damage check is a boss are what this page is for; floors whose check is density are not, and the base build will beat it there by a wide margin. Pick the page to match the floor.

Skill point priority

  1. Everything maxed
  2. Defensive floor: standing in a boss fight is not what this archetype was designed for and the base build's mobility was carrying more of its survival than it looks
  3. Aspect of Forest Power's larger barrier (20% to 30% of maximum life) and doubled armor (20-30% to 40-60%) are worth more here than in the base build for the same reason

Board & glyph focus

Glyph level order, published as an ordered list and identical in every variant: Consumption, Canny, Fester, Bane, Menagerist. The board strategy is a rush - 'one of the most efficient strategies is to rush to get your Legendary nodes even before you slot in glyphs. You will obtain the power spike from these faster than you will focusing on glyphs'. Prodigy's Tempo is the named build-requirement board at this stage. Spirit Halls here are Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary; Gorilla primary is one of the two Barrier sources, alongside the Tzic rune. Do not use the Colossal glyph - the guide removed it after finding it does not work properly with the swarm's damage-over-time.

How to run them

Identical across all eight of the guide's variants, and quoted almost verbatim: hire Subo 'for his map hacks and increased damage from Scorched Earth & Incendiary Bolt', reinforce with Raheir's Bastion 'for additional DR & Unstoppable'. The map visibility is not a luxury on a build whose entire point is crossing a map as fast as possible, and Bastion is doing the survivability work that a build with no defensive skill on the bar cannot do for itself.

Plan

Activity-level advice, re-weighted rather than invented. No Spiritborn guide publishes War Plan picks - the base build's planner payload carries none - so these are Maxroll's build-agnostic endgame progression priorities, reordered so that four of the nine sit in the Lair Bosses tree, which is the content this variant exists for. No `level` is recorded because no source publishes an order.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.

Loot filter

maxroll.gg
Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter (in-guide import code)

The base build's own in-guide filter, unchanged, because the affix pool is identical - cooldown reduction, damage over time, poison. One check before importing: this variant wears Widow's Web for the whole run rather than only in the early endgame, so make sure the code is not hiding amulets once you are past the stage it was tuned for. InfinityBuilds also publishes an S14 Spiritborn universal filter (leveling + endgame) if you want a second opinion.

Summary

The class's S-tier build, re-cut for the one thing every source agrees it is bad at. The 3.1.2 class snapshot's whole comment on Spiritborn is 'excels at speed with Evade Counterswarm but weaker at bossing', and Icy Veins ranks the class S for levelling and speed farming but only A for endgame push for the same reason. Nothing in this variant changes the engine - it is still Pestilent Swarms created by Counterattack running Counterattack of the Swarm, with Rushing Claw as a pure movement skill - but every optional choice is resolved toward a single target instead of a pack. Harmony of Ebewaka goes on from the early endgame rather than at the late endgame, which moves the Spirit Hall pairing to Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary early; Widow's Web stays on the amulet for the whole run; and the polearm rule is treated as non-negotiable. The trade is that pack clear gets slower and the character stops being a speed-farmer, which is the thing the base build is actually best in the game at. Two bug warnings carry over unchanged and both matter more here: the build deliberately uses Tzic for the 6x damage bug on unstoppable enemies and bosses, which is exactly the content this variant is built for, and the class-wide Spirit tag inheritance bug still makes charm +Ranks not work.

Reasoning

Based onEvade Counterswarm Spiritborn
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. Harmony of Ebewaka replaces Loyalty's Mantle from the early endgame instead of at the late endgame. The base guide's Spirit Hall pairing is item-driven rather than preference: Loyalty's Mantle forces Jaguar primary and Jaguar secondary because of the inheritance bug, and Harmony of Ebewaka moves you to Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary. Making that move earlier costs some early clear and buys the boss pairing sooner.
  2. Widow's Web stays on the amulet at every endgame stage. The base build wears it only in the early endgame; here the crit-chance floor it exists to proc matters for longer, because a boss fight is long enough for a proc chance to matter and a pack is not.
  3. The polearm rule is enforced rather than noted. The guide measures a Glaive at 11%[x] and a Quarterstaff at 22%[x] behind a Polearm because base weapon damage is what matters and the faster weapons buy nothing - so this variant does not take the two Quarterstaff uniques, Sepazontec and Rod of Kepeleke, even though 3.1.x buffed both (Sepazontec 100-120% to 140-180%, Rod of Kepeleke 0.65-0.75% to 0.85-1.05%).
  4. Crit chance is carried a little further than the base build carries it. The class-wide inverted rule still holds - the damage is a damage-over-time and damage over time cannot crit - but Widow's Web is worn for longer here and it has to actually proc.
  5. The Colossal glyph stays out, permanently. It was removed from the base guide after being found not to work properly with the swarm's damage over time; a boss variant is exactly where someone would be tempted to re-add it.
  6. Adds a War Plans allocation the base build does not carry, weighted toward Lair Bosses and The Pit rather than the generic farming order.
